statements.action_statement: Resolved io.opentelemetry:opentelemetry-api is 1.60.1 (bundled by the Quarkus platform BOM io.quarkus.platform:quarkus-bom:3.37.2). The unbounded W3C-baggage memory allocation is fixed in 1.62.0, which is binary-incompatible with the OpenTelemetry extension Quarkus 3.37.2 ships (a force to 1.62.0 fails every service at boot with NoClassDefFoundError: io/opentelemetry/common/impl/ApiUsageLogger, verified and reverted in PR #1367), so remediation requires the Quarkus platform bump tracked in issue #1446. Compensating control: the `baggage` propagator only parses the W3C `baggage` header on the in-mesh trace-context path (Istio STRICT mTLS between services); the customer-facing edge does not accept or forward an attacker-supplied baggage header, so the oversized-baggage parse path is not reachable from untrusted input. Residual risk: medium-severity DoS only, no data exposure.

statements.impact_statement: The advisory's affected range is io.netty:netty-codec-dns >=4.2.0.Final and <=4.2.15.Final (4.2.x line only). The fleet resolves netty on the 4.1.x line (4.1.136.Final, pinned in openbank.dependency-vulnerability-pins.gradle.kts), which the advisory does not list as affected; the 4.2.x sighting in the dependency graph is the Gradle dependency-graph tooling classpath, not any service's runtime classpath.

statements.action_statement: Resolved org.hibernate.reactive:hibernate-reactive-core is 3.4.2.Final (bundled by the Quarkus platform BOM io.quarkus.platform:quarkus-bom:3.38.0; measured with `./gradlew :openbank-mcp-service:dependencies --configuration runtimeClasspath`). The advisory's affected range is [0, 4.2.1), so this version is in range. The vulnerable path is REACHABLE here, so no not_affected justification is defensible: com.openbank.mcp.infrastructure.persistence.AgentSessionRepository extends io.quarkus.hibernate.reactive.panache.kotlin.PanacheRepository over the reactive PostgreSQL pool, and it is driven from HTTP request handling (McpSessionResource /api/v1/mcp/sessions and CallerContextResolver on the /mcp tool-call path), which is exactly the advisory's precondition (an HTTP endpoint performing database operations, where a remote client closing the connection prematurely can leak a pooled connection). Remediation is a Quarkus platform bump, not an independent force: forcing hibernate-reactive-core:4.2.1.Final resolves and augments cleanly (quarkusBuild succeeds) but fails every @QuarkusTest at boot with NoSuchMethodError org.hibernate.loader.ast.internal.LoaderSelectBuilder.createSelect(...) — 4.2.x needs a newer Hibernate ORM than Quarkus 3.38.0 ships (measured on branch security/vex-cve-2025-14969 and reverted; the baseline suite is green). Tracked in issue #4533. Note the tracker cited by the other 44 component VEX docs for this CVE, issue #1446, is CLOSED — it landed the 3.37.2 -> 3.38.0 bump, which moved this artifact 3.4.1.Final -> 3.4.2.Final and did not cross the fix boundary. Compensating controls: this service depends only on openbank-libs-domain / openbank-libs-runtime, neither of which carries the fleet reactive-pool eviction defaults, so it did NOT inherit them; this change therefore also sets quarkus.datasource.reactive.idle-timeout=5M and max-lifetime=30M explicitly in its application.yaml (the values openbank-libs META-INF/microprofile-config.properties defines fleet-wide, issue #1682), bounding how long a pooled connection can survive so a leak condition ages out rather than persisting until a pod restart. Every REST endpoint requires an authenticated caller (quarkus-oidc; @RolesAllowed(ROLE_OPERATOR, ROLE_ADMIN) on the session endpoints), matching the advisory's PR:L. Residual risk: availability only — GHSA-frpp-8pwq-hjrx is rated MODERATE (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L, 4.3); no confidentiality or integrity impact, and the finding is below the CRITICAL/HIGH threshold the weekly Image rescan gate (#4422) acts on.
